issues.legal_issue: A liquidator may not use authority to continue a company’s business to give unused company premises to another person for income when that is not necessary for the beneficial winding up.
material_facts: The company was ordered to be wound up, and its business of operating prize-chit schemes stopped.
The liquidator took possession of the company’s office premises and sought court directions to give them to another person under a caretaker agreement.
The premises were not needed for the liquidator’s winding-up activities, and the liquidator was not carrying on the company’s business.
issues.conclusion: The court could not authorize the caretaker agreement; because the premises were not needed for winding-up, the liquidator had to surrender possession to the landlords.
issues.legal_principle: Section 457(1)(b) of the Companies Act, 1956 permits a liquidator, with the court’s sanction, to carry on the company’s business only so far as necessary for the beneficial winding up. The business carried on must be the company’s business, and the necessity for beneficial winding up is a jurisdictional fact. The court relied on In re Batey; Ex parte Emmanuel, [1881] 17 Ch. Division 35, and Panchmahals Steel Ltd. v. Universal Steel Traders, [1976] 46 Company Cases 706, for the limited purpose of this power.

rule.if: winding_up_case and company_business_has_stopped and premises_not_needed_for_winding_up and liquidator_sought_to_transfer_use

predicates.winding_up_case: The proceeding concerns a company that has been ordered to be wound up.
predicates.company_business_has_stopped: The company’s business stopped after the winding-up order, and the liquidator was not continuing that business.
predicates.premises_not_needed_for_winding_up: The liquidator did not need the premises to carry out the winding-up activities.
predicates.liquidator_sought_to_transfer_use: The liquidator sought authority to give another person use or possession of the premises.
predicates.liquidator_must_surrender_unneeded_premi: The liquidator must surrender premises that are not needed for winding-up rather than transfer their use to another person for income.

issues.definition: When a company in winding up has stopped its business, the premises are unnecessary for winding-up, and the liquidator seeks to transfer their use, the liquidator must surrender the premises.

issues.legal_issue: A caretaker-agreement label cannot be used to evade rent-control restrictions on a statutory tenant giving another person possession of premises that the tenant no longer needs.
material_facts: The company occupied the premises as a tenant and was treated as a statutory tenant under the rent-control law.
The company no longer needed the premises after its business stopped.
The liquidator gave another person exclusive use of the premises under a caretaker agreement in return for compensation.
The landlords challenged the arrangement as contrary to restrictions on giving possession by licence or sublease.
issues.conclusion: The caretaker agreement was an impermissible means of parting with possession, and the court could not authorize it as a way around the rent-control restrictions.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 13 and 15 of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, as amended in 1973, restrict a statutory tenant from giving possession by licence or sublease. A court must not permit a caretaker agreement to serve as a facade for evading those restrictions and earning money from premises the tenant no longer needs. Although the rent-control law is to be interpreted to protect tenants, that purpose does not justify using the law to enable unfair or impermissible use of the premises.

rule.if: rent_control_possession_dispute and tenant_has_statutory_possession and tenant_no_longer_needs_premises and third_party_given_exclusive_use_under_caretaker_label

predicates.rent_control_possession_dispute: The proceeding concerns possession of premises occupied under rent-control protection.
predicates.tenant_has_statutory_possession: The tenant holds possession under statutory tenancy protection.
predicates.tenant_no_longer_needs_premises: The tenant no longer requires the premises for its own use.
predicates.third_party_given_exclusive_use_under_ca: The tenant or its liquidator gives another person exclusive use of the premises under an agreement described as a caretaker arrangement.
predicates.court_must_not_authorize_evasive_caretak: The court must not authorize a caretaker arrangement used to evade restrictions on transferring possession.

issues.definition: If a statutory tenant no longer needs the premises and gives a third party exclusive use under a caretaker label, the court must not authorize that arrangement as a means of evading rent-control restrictions.
